task.title: Provider-first helper claim when preferred lane is busy

scope.owned_layer: Supervisor helper claim preferred lane dispatch logic and state-aware capacity check
scope.not_changing: Supervisor status persistence, worker execution loop, or config schema
scope.composes_with: Orchestrator dispatch policy and worker reassignment rules

supervisor_py: choose_helper_claim_agent: pass state=state to agent_can_take_task (was missing; capacity check silently skipped)
choose_helper_claim_agent: prefer preferred_fallbacks exclusively when task has preferred_lane_order (vs old append behaviour that let Codex2 in via owner_fallbacks)
choose_helper_claim_agent: fix priority comparison from < to <= so equal-priority loads correctly qualify
task_preferred_lane_blocks_helper_claim: always call task_next_preferred_helper_lane regardless of owner_paused; remove the path that fell through to a raw index comparison when owner was not paused
task_next_preferred_helper_lane: add owner_paused parameter; add state-aware capacity check so a lane at full capacity is skipped and the next available preferred lane is returned
test_supervisor_py: 20 new helper_claim unit tests covering: busy preferred lane defers to next available, full-capacity preferred lane skip, preferred_fallbacks overrides owner_fallbacks, priority comparison boundary, paused vs busy branching

commands.note: Full supervisor regression — no regressions introduced
